text: On October 12, 1492, Columbus arrived in the Americas, initiating the historic encounter between Europe and the New World.
description_end:
Christopher Columbus reached American shores, landing on a Caribbean island he named San Salvador.
This event marked the encounter between Europe and the Americas, launching the exploration and conquest of the New World.
It is considered the beginning of the Modern Age in world history.
hint_1: Sentence about Christopher Columbus and the discovery of the New World.

text: On July 20, 1969, humankind set foot on the Moon for the first time. When Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface, he pronounced the famous phrase: It’s one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.
description_end: The Apollo 11 moon landing realized a millennia‑old dream and proved the power of science, engineering, and international cooperation. Armstrong’s words symbolized the breaking of limits and, in the midst of the Cold War, consolidated technological leadership. It spurred advances in materials, computing, and telecommunications, inspired scientific vocations, and gave us a new view of Earth: fragile, shared, and without borders.
hint_1: Famous quote from the Apollo 11 moon landing.
hint_2: Words appearing in the sentence: man, small, mankind

text: On November 9, 1989, the Berlin Wall fell. Within hours, thousands of Berliners crossed the border checkpoints, embracing over the remains of the concrete. That event symbolized the end of the Cold War and opened the path to the reunification of Germany and a new Europe.
description_end: That night, the breakthrough happened at Bornholmer Straße. At the Bornholmer crossing, the duty chief Harald Jäger was overwhelmed by the crowd. Without clear orders and to avoid a tragedy, at 11:30 p.m. he made a historic decision: he lifted the barrier and let everyone pass without checks. It was the first open crossing of the night; afterward, the rest followed.
hint_1: The sentence revolves around the Berlin Wall.
hint_2: Words appearing in the sentence: Berlin, concrete, Germany, Europe

text: On July 14, 1789, the storming of the Bastille in Paris marked the beginning of the French Revolution. This event represented the people’s struggle against absolute monarchy and became a universal symbol of liberty, equality, and fraternity, inspiring generations to come.
description_end: The Bastille: a fortress‑prison of the Ancien Régime, its fall unleashed the Great Fear and pushed the Assembly to abolish feudal privileges on the night of August 4. Weeks later it approved the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen. Since 1880, July 14 has been a national holiday in France.
hint_1: The sentence describes an event with which the French Revolution began.
hint_2: Words appearing in the sentence: Bastille, monarchy, equality, later generations

text: In 1996, the sheep Dolly was born not by chance, but as evidence that an adult cell could reset its fate: cloning stepped out of the lab to plant a doubt; if we can copy life, what limits and responsibilities are we duplicating as a species?
description_end: Since then, cloning has refined its techniques: cellular reprogramming and iPS (induced pluripotent stem cells), advances in primates, and therapeutic aims. However, low efficiency, epigenetic errors, and malformation risks constrain it. Today it is tolerated for research and regenerative medicine, not to copy people.
hint_1: The most famous sheep in history, born in a laboratory as a result of cloning.
hint_2: Words present in the quote: Dolly, cloning, responsibilities

text: The principle of AI is simple yet profound: turning experience into prediction. It observes data, detects patterns, generalizes, and decides under uncertainty. Between search, learning, and representation, it models the world to help us choose better—not to stop us from thinking.
description_end: But every prediction is a bet: it depends on data quality, context, bias, and the goal we define. That’s why the principle is completed by another: transparency and human oversight—knowing when to trust, when to correct, and when to stop a system so that it expands judgment, not replaces it.
hint_1: A thought about technology and the origin and purpose of AI.
hint_2: Words in the sentence: AI, world, patterns, thinking

text: In September 1914, during the First World War, German troops were forced to retreat behind the Marne River, near Paris. This withdrawal marked a decisive turning point: many historians agree it was the moment Germany lost the war.
description_end: This retreat thwarted the German plan to take Paris in a few weeks and forced a change of strategy that began trench warfare. The Western Front stagnated for years, with enormous human losses and no significant advances until the final outcome.
hint_1: Anniversary about the First World War.
hint_2: Words in the sentence: German, trenches, human.

text: In 9 AD, Arminius led an alliance of Germanic tribes that ambushed in the Teutoburg Forest, annihilating three Roman legions under Varus. From then on, Rome halted its expansion toward Germania, fixing its borders at the Rhine.
description_end: The defeat at Teutoburg had profound consequences for Rome: it definitively halted expansion northward, fixed the frontier at the Rhine, and consolidated the identity of the Germanic tribes. From then on, Germania remained outside the direct control of the Roman Empire.

text: In 1941 the Nazi siege of Leningrad began, lasting almost 900 days. The population, without food or heating, survived on sawdust bread while working in improvised factories. 650,000 people died, but the resistance was decisive in stopping Hitler.
description_end: The extreme suffering and the iron will of the inhabitants symbolized Soviet fortitude. The siege, finally broken in 1944, marked a key turn in the Second World War and strengthened Soviet morale, granting Leningrad a place of honor in historical memory.

text: In 1380, on the banks of the Don River, the Muscovite prince Dmitry Donskoy led the Russians against the Mongol Tatars. The victory—despite 70,000 own casualties and 130,000 enemy losses—unified Russia and marked the beginning of the decline of Mongol rule.
description_end: The victory at Kulikovo strengthened Moscow’s leadership and created a symbol of unity against foreign invasion. Although Tatar domination persisted for decades, the battle was seen as the first step toward Russian independence and the consolidation of Muscovite power.
